correctness.rationale: For any finite H≤S_n, n≥4, fixed barycentric coordinates of an H-invariant point are constant on each edge orbit; only orbit-faces consisting of mutually meeting K_n edges survive. A pairwise-intersecting edge set is contained in a star or the three edges of a triangle; orbit transitivity forces unique fixed star centers or internal size-2 and size-3 vertex orbits. The star-simplex cover on a fixed vertices has pairwise singleton intersections; filled triangles on fixed triples recover sk₂(Δ^{a−1}), yielding binom(a−1,3) integral 2-spheres. Every size-2 orbit adds a vertex linked to each of a stars, yielding b(a−1) independent circles; size-3 orbits remain c isolated points. If a=0 only b+c isolated points remain. This establishes the geometric (not vertexwise) fixed locus for all subgroups, including noncyclic. Independently rebuilt the orbit-barycenter complexes and mod-2 chain ranks for 97 subgroup examples (n=4,5,6), all agreeing; finite mod-2 tests do not supply the integral all-H proof.

originality.rationale: QUALIFIED PASS. Goyal–Shukla–Singh Lemma 3.2 establishes the ordinary, nonequivariant homotopy equivalence Cl(L(G))≃sk₂ Cl(G). This does not commute with taking arbitrary subgroup geometric fixed points without an equivariant argument, and does not give the explicit (a,b,c)-dependent fixed-point decomposition, empty/disconnected loci, or first-homology circles. The new edge-orbit classification supplies the missing equivariant information. Equivalent equivariant nerves or historical nonmatching-complex results remain conceivable; no search failure is treated as priority certification.

Finite mod-two experiments do not independently certify the all-subgroup integral homotopy argument.

It can serve in equivariant obstruction, Euler-character and subgroup-comparison calculations.
